Explain how a VPN works in simple words
9:17 PM

A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and another computer on the internet, and everything you send goes through it scrambled.

Without a VPN, websites see your device's address, and your internet provider or a public Wi-Fi owner can see where your traffic goes. With a VPN, your data is locked before it leaves your device and travels to the VPN company's computer. That computer unlocks it and sends it on to the website, so the site sees the VPN's address, not yours.

That's why people use it on public Wi-Fi, to keep snoopers out, or to appear to be in another city or country. It doesn't make you invisible, though. The VPN company can still see your traffic, so pick one you trust.
